summary: When His mother and brothers come asking for Him, Jesus points to His disciples and says that whoever does God’s will is His true family.
key_insight: Jesus does not disown His mother and brothers; He widens the family. The way in is not birth but doing the will of God, which means the door stands open to anyone, including His own relatives.
story: While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, His mother and brothers arrived. {Mt} They could not get near Him because of the crowd, {Lk} so they stood outside and sent word in, calling for Him. {Mk}
A crowd was sitting around Him, and someone told Him, “Look, Your mother and Your brothers are outside seeking You.” {Mk}

Jesus answered, “Who is My mother, or My brothers?” {Mk} He looked around at those sitting in a circle about Him, {Mk} stretched out His hand toward His disciples, {Mt} and said, “Here are My mother and My brothers! For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother.” {Mt}
His mother and brothers, He said, are “these who hear the word of God and do it.” {Lk}
differences: Mark ties the family’s arrival to his earlier note that Jesus’ own people set out to take hold of Him, saying He was out of His mind (3:21), with the Beelzebub dispute in between.
Matthew says Jesus stretched out His hand toward His disciples; Mark says He looked around at those who sat about Him.
Jesus’ words vary: “the will of My Father in heaven” (Matthew), “the will of God” (Mark), and “hear the word of God and do it” (Luke).
Matthew and Mark place the scene before the parables by the sea; Luke places it after the parable of the sower.

fit.question: Matthew and Mark tell this scene before the parable of the sower; Luke tells it after. Which order is right?

points.label: The same day
points.text: Matthew ties the two scenes together. The family arrives while Jesus is still speaking (12:46), and “On the same day” He goes out to the sea and teaches in parables (13:1). Both happened on one day.

points.label: Luke groups by theme
points.text: Luke places the family scene right after “take heed how you hear” (8:18). Jesus’ words about those who “hear the word of God and do it” complete that teaching, so Luke sets them side by side.

fit.note: The scenes happened on one day; Luke groups them for meaning without changing what happened.
fit.short: Matthew says both scenes happened the same day. Luke places the family scene after the sower to link it with hearing and doing God’s word.

scene.label: His brothers
scene.text: Mark 6:3 names four brothers, James, Joses, Judas and Simon, and mentions sisters. Most Protestants understand them as children born to Mary and Joseph after Jesus. Catholic and Orthodox Christians, who hold that Mary remained a virgin, understand them as cousins or as Joseph’s sons from an earlier marriage.

scene.label: Brothers who came to believe
scene.text: During His ministry “even His brothers did not believe in Him” (John 7:5). After the resurrection Jesus appeared to James (1 Corinthians 15:7), and His brothers were found praying with the disciples (Acts 1:14). James later led the church in Jerusalem.

scene.label: Family loyalty
scene.text: In Jesus’ world, family came first, and a son owed his mother honor. A teacher who pointed past his own mother in public would have startled the crowd. Jesus did honor Mary; from the cross He provided for her care (John 19:26–27).

witnesses.matthew: Places the scene at the end of chapter 12, right after Jesus warns an evil generation. Matthew’s “My Father in heaven” makes the point clear: those who do His Father’s will belong to Jesus’ family.
witnesses.mark: Has already told that Jesus’ own people thought He was out of His mind (3:21), so the family’s arrival carries tension. Mark adds the vivid detail of Jesus looking around at the circle of listeners seated about Him.
witnesses.luke: Places the scene after the parable of the sower and the call to “take heed how you hear.” Jesus’ answer, “these who hear the word of God and do it,” shows what the good ground looks like in real people.

seeing.reveals: Jesus is forming a new family around Himself, bound not by birth but by doing the will of His Father. He calls ordinary disciples His brother, sister and mother.
seeing.living: No one is born into this family, and no one is kept out of it by birth. Anyone who hears God’s word and does it belongs to Jesus. That also makes the people sitting with you around Him your family.
seeing.ponder: Do you think of Jesus as someone you admire from a distance, or as the One who calls you family because you do His Father’s will?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus’ family is made not by blood but by hearing and doing the Father’s will.
outline: A question that redraws the circle (33)
preaching.watch_for: Mark says twice that the family stood “outside” (vv. 31–32), while the crowd sat around Jesus. Where people stand in relation to Jesus becomes the point: who is inside His circle, and on what basis.
